Not exactly on the "road", but the thing that cemented my love for coffee in my friends minds was when we were sitting on the top of Mt. Fuji waiting for sunrise to come. It was dark and cold and as we were shivering at 3am I started to unpack an alcohol stove and a small moka pot. I ended up making coffee for everyone in my group and the group next to us. I got a little flak for bringing as much coffee as I did while we were packing but I didn't hear any complaints at the top. A hot cup of coffee in hand while watching the sunrise from the top of Fuji will forever be in my memory.

Personally I'd say it's one of the best preground coffees you can get, but keep in mind it's still preground and ground coffee goes stale really quickly. It's definitely a step up from nescafe but if you really want to improve your morning cup I would suggest grinding your own.
How often do you grind your own thats non-bustelo?

Oh I grind fresh every time. Once you start grinding fresh you can never go back. My mother hates me because of this she says ever since I got her a grinder she can't enjoy preground anymore even though its so much more convenient.
LOL a blessing and a curse for your mom.

I know a lot of people enjoy it. Personally though, I don't use anything preground. It's inferior to freshly ground coffee in every way except price and convenience. If you're more interested in price and convenience than quality, then this is one of the better options.

If you don't mind spending a bit more because you want better coffee, freshly roasted and freshly ground beans will be like unlocking a new world. Pick up a refurbished Baratza Encore and an Aeropress, french press or maybe a pour over cone (Though pour over can be tricky for newbies.). After that, find a reputable local roaster. If you can't find any, I can fully endorse HappyMugCoffee.com for fairly inexpensive coffee that is still high quality. Once you get the hang of it, maybe try some higher end roasters like Chromatic, Stumptown, Intelligentsia etc.

When it comes down to it, just about anything you're going to get in a grocery store will be low quality commodity coffee that is far from fresh. Some higher end stores like Whole Foods are starting to carry stuff from Intelligentsia and others, but by the time it hits the shelves it's usually already stale. If you want the best cup you can get, you have to look towards "specialty" coffee (Though I dislike the term.).

BUT, some people are perfectly happy with commodity coffee, and that's okay. If you like it, drink it. If you want to get into the deeper world of coffee, the rabbit hole goes far deeper than most people realize.
